newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus to purchase oil from Iraq - official.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus to purchase oil from Iraq - official.

text.p: Cyprus has applied for United Nations permission to buy 110,000 tonnes of crude oil from Iraq, a representative of the Commerce Ministry said on Monday.
Approval could mean delivery as early as April, Solon Kassinis of the island's Commerce, Industry and Tourism Ministry told Reuters.
He said the price per barrel would be $1.55 below the international benchmark North Sea Brent Crude rate.
"This is subject to the approval by the United Nations, under resolution 986," Kassinis said, adding that the contract has been sent to New York for ratification.
Kassinis was part of an official five-member delegation in Baghdad last week for talks with Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation.

The "oil-for-food" agreement, which took effect on December 10, permits Iraq to sell 2 billion dollars worth of oil over six months to buy humanitarian needs to offset the effects of trade sanctions imposed after its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Cyprus has been buying most of its crude from Russia but before Iraqi exports came under sanctions Cyprus had bought an average of around 600,000 tonnes of Iraqi oil per year.
